Goopaws 4-in-1 Self Warming Pet Bed: Features, Sizes, Pros and Cons, and Buying Guide

By Designbeep Staff October 15, 2026

Goopaws 4-in-1 Self Warming Pet Bed

Cats and small dogs spend most of the day asleep, and they are picky about where they do it. They want warmth, softness, and a place to hide. The Goopaws 4-in-1 self warming pet bed tries to offer all three in one low-cost product. It folds and zips into different shapes, so one bed can serve as a mat, a cup-shaped bed, a pod, or a covered cave.

This guide explains what the bed is, how each mode works, what it is made of, how big it is, and how to care for it. It also covers the pros and cons, how it compares with electric heated pads, and how to decide whether it suits your pet.

A note on method: this guide is based on the product’s published details and listings from major pet retailers, not on a hands-on test. Details such as price, colors, and sizes can change, so check the current listing before you buy.

What Is It?

The Goopaws 4-in-1 self warming pet bed is a soft, padded mat with fasteners that let you shape it. Laid flat, it is a plush mat. Raise and fasten the edges, and it becomes a bed with walls. Pull the top over, and it becomes a semi-enclosed cave or burrow. The same item adapts to the season, the pet, and the place you want to put it.

The brand sells it at large pet retailers and online marketplaces. Retailers list it under names such as “4-in-1 Cat Burrow Cave Bed” with “self-warming” in the title.

The Four Modes

Mode Shape Best For
Flat mat A soft, open pad Warm weather, crates, carriers, sofas, and car seats
Open bed Raised edges around a soft center Pets that curl up and like to rest their head on a bolster
Pod or cup Higher sides with a partial cover Pets that like to feel hugged but still see out
Cave A covered burrow with a wide opening Cold weather, shy pets, and animals that love to hide

Cats often change their favorite sleeping style with the seasons. A convertible design lets you follow those changes without buying a new bed.

How Does Self-Warming Work?

The term can be confusing. A self-warming bed has no heater, no cord, and no batteries. It works by trapping the heat your pet’s body already makes.

Two things do the work.

  1. Insulation. The thick fill and long faux fur hold a layer of warm air around the animal, much as a down jacket does for a person.
  2. Enclosure. In cave mode, the cover holds in warm air that would otherwise rise and escape.

Some self-warming products also add a thin reflective layer, like an emergency blanket, which sends body heat back toward the pet. Check the listing for the specific bed you buy to see how it is built.

The effect is gentle. A self-warming bed will feel cozy within a few minutes of use, but it will not feel hot to your hand like an electric pad. That is the point. It cannot overheat, and it uses no power.

Materials and Comfort

  • Faux rabbit fur exterior. The surface is long, soft, and plush. Many cats knead this kind of fabric, since it feels like fur.
  • Soft fill. The padding cushions joints and adds insulation.
  • Semi-enclosed design. The makers describe the cave as balanced, so it keeps warmth in without trapping too much heat.
  • Light weight. The bed is easy to move from room to room or to pack for travel.

Long faux fur does hold on to shed hair, so expect to shake it out or vacuum it between washes.

Size and Fit

The listed size is about 21 by 17 inches when flat, with a thickness of about 3 inches. In cave or bed mode, the usable space inside is smaller than the flat size.

Pet Fit
Kittens Roomy
Average adult cats, up to about 12 pounds Good fit in all modes
Large cats, such as Maine Coons May be snug in cave mode. Better as a mat or open bed
Toy and small dogs, up to about 12 to 15 pounds Good fit
Medium and large dogs Too small
Rabbits, ferrets, and guinea pigs Can work, with supervision for chewers

How to measure your pet:

  1. Measure from the nose to the base of the tail while your pet is lying in a relaxed position.
  2. Add 4 to 6 inches for a pet that stretches out.
  3. For a pet that curls into a ball, measure the widest point of the curl.
  4. Compare with the listed size.

If your pet is near the top of the range, plan to use it mainly as a mat or open bed.

For medium and large dogs, look at a bigger, more supportive bed instead. Our review of the PetFusion Ultimate Dog Bed With Memory Foam covers one popular option for larger breeds and older dogs with stiff joints.

Care and Cleaning

The Goopaws 4-in-1 self warming pet bed is listed as machine washable. Follow the care label on your own bed, since instructions can differ. As a general approach for faux fur beds:

  1. Shake the bed out and remove loose hair with a lint roller or vacuum.
  2. Close any zippers or fasteners.
  3. Wash on a gentle cycle in cold or cool water with a mild, unscented detergent.
  4. Skip bleach and fabric softener. Softener can mat the fibers and leave a scent that cats dislike.
  5. Tumble dry on low heat or air dry. High heat can melt or mat faux fur.
  6. Fluff the fur with your hands or a soft brush once it is dry.

Wash the bed every one to two weeks, or more often for pets with allergies or skin problems.

Self-Warming Beds vs. Electric Heating Pads

Many owners weigh a self warming cat bed against a heating pad for cats. They solve the same problem in different ways.

Feature Self-Warming Bed Electric Pet Heating Pad
Heat source The pet’s own body heat Electricity
Warmth level Gentle Warmer, often set to match a pet’s body temperature
Running cost None A small amount of electricity
Safety No cord or heating element Needs a chew-resistant cord, a thermostat, and regular checks
Where it can go Anywhere Near an outlet
Best for Healthy pets, mild chill, travel, and unsupervised use Senior pets, very cold rooms, and short-haired or thin pets
Typical price Lower Higher

A pet heating pad can be a great help for an older cat with stiff joints or for a pet in an unheated room. If you choose one, pick a model made for animals, with a low fixed temperature, a chew-resistant cord, and a safety certification. Never use a pad that was designed for people as a heating pad for cats. Human pads run much hotter and can burn a pet that cannot or will not move away.

You can also combine the two. Some owners slide a low-wattage pet heating pad under a mat or bed in the coldest months. Only do so if the pad’s instructions allow it, and never fold a pad or cover it in a way the maker warns against.

For most healthy indoor pets in a heated home, a self warming cat bed gives enough comfort without any of those concerns.

Who Should Buy It?

The Goopaws 4-in-1 self warming pet bed suits some pets far better than others.

It is a good fit for:

  • Cats that love to burrow under blankets
  • Shy or anxious pets that feel safer in an enclosed space
  • Small dogs that get cold easily, such as Chihuahuas and Yorkshire terriers
  • Homes with cool floors or drafty rooms
  • Owners who want a low-cost bed that works all year
  • Travel, crates, and carriers, in mat mode

It may not suit:

  • Large cats and any dog over about 15 pounds
  • Heavy chewers and teething puppies
  • Pets with incontinence, since no waterproof layer is listed
  • Senior pets with arthritis that need firm, orthopedic support or real heat
  • Owners who want a bed with rigid walls

How to Get Your Pet to Use It

Cats can be suspicious of new things. These steps help.

  1. Pick the right spot. Place the bed where your pet already likes to sleep: a sunny window, the sofa, or a quiet corner.
  2. Add a familiar scent. Put a worn T-shirt or your pet’s old blanket inside.
  3. Start in an open mode. Many pets accept a mat or open bed sooner than a cave. Change the shape once they use it.
  4. Use treats and toys. Place a few treats or a sprinkle of catnip or silvervine on the bed.
  5. Raise it up. Cats often prefer a bed on a chair or shelf to one on the floor.
  6. Do not force it. Putting a cat into a bed can make it avoid the bed.
  7. Give it time. Some pets need a week or two.

Safety Tips

  • Check the bed often for loose threads, torn seams, and exposed filling.
  • Take it away from pets that chew or swallow fabric.
  • Supervise puppies and kittens at first.
  • Keep the bed away from space heaters, radiators, and fireplaces.
  • Make sure your pet can leave the cave easily.
  • Replace the bed if the filling clumps badly or the cover tears.

Other Beds to Consider

If this one does not fit your pet, another style may. A firm felt cave, a thermal mat, or a different self warming cat bed could be a better match.

Type Good For Trade-Off
Donut or calming bed Pets that curl up No cover
Felt or wool cave Cats that like firm walls Higher price, usually not machine washable
Thermal mat with reflective layer Crates and carriers Thin, little cushioning
Orthopedic foam bed Senior pets Less cozy, costs more
Heated bed with thermostat Cold rooms and older pets Needs power and regular checks
Window perch Cats that love to watch outside Not enclosed

Buying Tips

A little care at checkout helps you avoid a return.

  • Buy from a known retailer, and compare the listed size across sellers. Similar beds from the same brand are sold in more than one size.
  • Read recent reviews for comments on how the shape holds up after washing.
  • Check the return policy, since pets have their own opinions.
  • Choose a color that hides your pet’s fur if hair bothers you.
  • Have a spare bed or blanket on hand for wash days.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does the Goopaws 4-in-1 self warming pet bed need to be plugged in? No. It has no electrical parts. It holds in your pet’s own body heat.

What are the four modes? A flat mat, an open bed with raised sides, a pod, and a covered cave.

Is it machine washable? It is listed as machine washable. Follow the care label.

How big is it? About 21 by 17 inches when flat.

Is it good for dogs? Yes, for small dogs. It is too small for medium and large breeds.

Is a self-warming bed safe to leave out all day? Yes. With no heating element, it cannot overheat.

Will it keep my cat warm outdoors? It is designed for indoor use. Outdoor and feral cats need a weatherproof shelter with straw.

Is it warm enough for a senior cat? It adds comfort. An older cat with arthritis may benefit more from a low-wattage heating pad for cats or a heated bed made for pets. Ask your vet.

How long does it last? That depends on your pet and how often you wash it. Soft beds of this kind often last one to two years with regular use.

Final Thoughts

The Goopaws 4-in-1 self warming pet bed offers a lot for a small price: a soft faux fur surface, four shapes for different seasons and moods, gentle warmth with no power, and easy washing. It suits cats and small dogs that love to burrow, hide, or curl up somewhere soft.

It is not for every pet. Large animals will not fit, heavy chewers may destroy it, and old or unwell pets may need firmer support or real heat. If your pet is small, healthy, and fond of cozy hiding places, this bed is a simple way to give it a warm spot all year.

Key Takeaways

  • The Goopaws 4-in-1 self warming pet bed converts between a mat, an open bed, a pod, and a covered cave.
  • It uses insulation and a semi-enclosed shape to hold in body heat, with no cord or batteries.
  • The listed size is about 21 by 17 inches, which fits most cats and small dogs up to about 12 to 15 pounds.
  • It has a faux rabbit fur exterior, a soft fill, and a machine-washable design.
  • Self-warming beds give gentle warmth, while electric pads made for pets give more heat for seniors and cold rooms.
  • Never use a human heating pad for a pet.
  • Introduce the bed in a favorite spot with a familiar scent, and check it often for wear.
